The draft statement considers only the simplistic alternatives of opening all lands or closing all lands to ORV use; it ignores the entire range of possible actions which would allow controlled use in limited areas, and dispenses of the entire problem in only six pages of discussion. This is entirely inadequate to satisfy the NEPA requirement that agencies give substantial consideration to alternative courses of action.
III. What the Secretary should do.
In order to rectify the inadequacies in the current Draft
Statement, the Secretary should withdraw it completely and issue
a new draft statement. Ordinarily, inadequacies could be corrected\nin a final impact statement. However, the present statement is so\ninadequate in discussing environmental impacts and alternatives
and its purpose is so unclear that the whole process should begin
again. The Secretary should at the same time reissue his
memorandum with the following revisions:
(1) Ban all ORV use in National Parks, Monuments, Reservations, National Wildlife Refuges; and any other Federal areas that are administered by the Interior Department primarily for wildlife conservation purposes.
(2) Direct bureau heads to ban ORV use in areas where it would conflict substantially with other recreational uses which are less harmful to the environment, and in areas where it would cause serious environmental damage.*
*
The ORRV Task Force Report states on p. 46 that the Bureau of Land Management has already closed all lands in Southern California where serious environmental degredation is occurring, pending the outcome of studies to determine the uses that the land can sustain.
